subject: Mathematics

about: VCE, Data, finance, matrices and networks
syllabus: VCE Mathematics Study Design (from 2023), General Mathematics Units 3 and 4

units.title: Unit 3: Data analysis, and recursion and financial modelling

points.title: Displaying data
points.brief: Two-way tables, segmented bar charts, dot plots, stem plots and histograms, with a log base 10 scale for data over several powers of ten.

points.title: Describing a distribution
points.brief: A distribution is described by its shape, centre (median or mean), spread (IQR or standard deviation) and any outliers.

points.title: Boxplots and outliers
points.brief: Outliers lie below Q1 − 1.5 × IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 × IQR, and are drawn as separate points on a boxplot.

points.title: The 68-95-99.7 rule
points.brief: For a bell-shaped distribution, about 68%, 95% and 99.7% of values lie within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations of the mean.

points.title: Standardised scores
points.brief: A z-score is (x − mean) ÷ standard deviation, the number of standard deviations a value lies from the mean.

points.title: Comparing with z-scores
points.brief: z-scores let values from different distributions be compared, such as marks on two tests.

points.title: Response and explanatory variables
points.brief: The explanatory variable may explain changes in the response variable, and goes on the horizontal axis.

points.title: Associations between categorical variables
points.brief: In a two-way table, an association exists when percentages for one variable differ across the other.

points.title: A numerical and a categorical variable
points.brief: Back-to-back stem plots, parallel dot plots and boxplots show whether a numerical variable differs across groups.

points.title: Pearson's correlation coefficient
points.brief: r measures the strength and direction of a linear association, from −1 to 1. It is only meaningful for linear data.

points.title: Correlation and causation
points.brief: A correlation does not show cause. Only a controlled experiment, not observation alone, can show that one variable causes another.

points.title: The least squares regression line
points.brief: The line y = a + bx that makes the sum of squared residuals smallest. The slope b = r × sy/sx.

points.title: Interpreting slope and intercept
points.brief: The slope is the change in the response for each unit increase in the explanatory variable; the intercept is its value when that is zero.

points.title: The coefficient of determination
points.brief: r² gives the percentage of variation in the response explained by the explanatory variable.

points.title: Residuals and residual plots
points.brief: A residual is actual minus predicted. A residual plot with no pattern supports a linear model.

points.title: Data transformations
points.brief: Squaring, taking the logarithm or the reciprocal of a variable can straighten a curved scatterplot before fitting a line.

points.title: Features of a time series
points.brief: A time series plot may show trend, seasonality, cycles, irregular fluctuations, structural change and outliers.

points.title: Smoothing with moving means
points.brief: Replacing each value with the mean of it and its neighbours smooths out fluctuations. Even-numbered means need centring.

points.title: Median smoothing
points.brief: Replacing each value with the median of it and its neighbours, often done on the graph, which resists outliers.

points.title: Seasonal indices
points.brief: A seasonal index compares a season with the average season. An index of 1.2 means 20% above average.

points.title: Deseasonalising data
points.brief: Dividing each value by its seasonal index removes seasonality so the trend is clearer.

points.title: Forecasting from a trend
points.brief: Fit a least squares line to deseasonalised data, predict, then reseasonalise by multiplying by the seasonal index.

points.title: Recurrence relations for finance
points.brief: A first-order linear recurrence, V(n+1) = R × V(n) + d, models balances growing or shrinking each period.

points.title: Flat-rate depreciation
points.brief: An asset loses the same amount each period, V(n+1) = V(n) − d, a linear decay.

points.title: Unit cost depreciation
points.brief: An asset loses value by a fixed amount for each unit of use, such as per kilometre driven.

points.title: Reducing balance depreciation
points.brief: An asset loses a fixed percentage each period, so its value decays geometrically.

points.title: Simple and compound interest in Unit 3
points.brief: Simple interest adds the same amount each period; compound interest adds a percentage of the growing balance. Recurrence relations model both.

points.title: Effective annual interest rate
points.brief: The yearly rate that gives the same growth as a nominal rate compounded more often. More frequent compounding raises it.

points.title: Reducing balance loans
points.brief: A loan where interest is added each period and a regular repayment comes off, until the balance reaches zero.

points.title: Amortisation tables
points.brief: A table showing each payment, the interest, the reduction in principal and the balance, step by step.

points.title: Annuities
points.brief: An investment that pays out regular amounts until it runs out, its balance falling each period.

points.title: Perpetuities
points.brief: An investment that pays out only the interest each period, so the balance never falls.

points.title: Compound interest with regular additions
points.brief: An investment that earns interest and also has a regular amount added each period.

points.title: Using a finance solver
points.brief: A finance solver finds any one of N, I%, PV, PMT and FV from the others, with money in and out given opposite signs.

units.title: Unit 4: Matrices, and networks and decision mathematics

points.title: Types of matrices
points.brief: Row, column, square, diagonal, symmetric, triangular, zero, binary and identity matrices, and the transpose.

points.title: Matrix arithmetic
points.brief: Adding, subtracting, scalar multiplying and multiplying matrices, and checking the orders allow it.

points.title: Building a matrix from a rule
points.brief: A rule for the element in row i and column j, such as 2i + j, builds a whole matrix.

points.title: Determinants and inverses
points.brief: The determinant shows whether a square matrix has an inverse, which undoes its multiplication.

points.title: Binary and permutation matrices
points.brief: Matrices of 0s and 1s record links or yes-no data. A permutation matrix reorders the rows or columns of another.

points.title: Communication and dominance matrices
points.brief: Matrices showing who can contact whom, or who beat whom, where adding powers counts two-step links.

points.title: Transition matrices
points.brief: A matrix whose columns give the chances of moving between states, used to predict a population's states over time.

points.title: Steady state
points.brief: After many steps, a regular transition matrix leads to a steady state where the numbers in each state stop changing.

points.title: Matrix recurrence relations
points.brief: S(n+1) = T × S(n) gives each state matrix from the one before, and a column can be added each step.

points.title: Leslie matrices
points.brief: A matrix model of a population by age group, using birth rates and survival rates to project the population.

points.title: Culling and restocking
points.brief: Adding or subtracting a matrix at each step extends a matrix recurrence to populations that are culled or restocked.

points.title: Graph terms
points.brief: Vertices, edges, degree, planar graphs and Euler's rule, directed graphs (digraphs) and weighted networks.

points.title: Adjacency matrices
points.brief: A matrix showing how many edges join each pair of vertices.

points.title: Eulerian trails and Hamiltonian paths
points.brief: An Eulerian trail uses every edge once; a Hamiltonian path visits every vertex once. Vertex degrees show when an Eulerian trail or circuit exists.

points.title: Trees and spanning trees
points.brief: A tree is a connected graph with no cycles. A spanning tree includes every vertex of a graph.

points.title: Prim's algorithm
points.brief: Build a minimum spanning tree by repeatedly adding the cheapest edge that joins a new vertex to the tree.

points.title: Dijkstra's algorithm
points.brief: Find the shortest path from one vertex by fixing the closest unvisited vertex each step.

points.title: Flow networks and minimum cut
points.brief: The maximum flow through a network equals the capacity of its minimum cut.

points.title: The Hungarian algorithm
points.brief: A bipartite graph or table sets out a matching problem, and the Hungarian algorithm assigns people or machines to tasks at least cost.

points.title: Activity networks
points.brief: A precedence table becomes an activity network, with dummy activities where needed to show what must come first.

points.title: Earliest and latest start times
points.brief: A forward scan finds earliest start times, and a backward scan finds the latest start times.

points.title: The critical path and float
points.brief: Activities with zero float form the critical path, which sets the minimum time for the project.

points.title: Crashing a project
points.brief: Shortening some activities, at a cost, to cut the project time, which may change the critical path.
